clue.text: It will probably never be finished in truth — hard one? Bloody impossible!

definitions.text: It will probably never be finished

indicators.note: impossible suggests the words cannot stand as they are, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exasperated grumble that some truth or task is so hard it will never be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impossible' rearranges TRUTH, HARD, ONE and BLOODY, all eighteen letters, into the four-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom warns someone not to wait expectantly, since the thing awaited is unlikely ever to happen or be finished.

clue.text: See 22 across
Lift someone with a whistle, I say, seeing dancer

indicators.note: in a down clue, to lift a piece is to raise it, so its letters read upwards in reverse

parts.note: a referee blows a whistle; REF is the short form
OOH is an exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: Someone hoisting a referee, with a posh exclamation, on spotting a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' turns REF and OOH together, giving HOOFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for a professional stage performer of tap or chorus routines.

clue.text: Try these hot surfaces, initially, as warm places

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the three words after it

explanation.surface: An invitation to touch some hot surfaces that are said to be warm places.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireplaces are the warm spots of a home, where the fire is lit.

clue.text: Change around a short clue for the card game

indicators.note: around says one piece is placed so as to surround the others

parts.note: loose change is coins, such as pence

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework a brief crossword clue so it describes a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: The solitaire card game played alone is known in Britain by this name.

clue.text: Wearing jumper, mother has splashed out so to be warmer in winter?

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the jumper's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a jumper is a top, a knitted garment
MA is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: splashed suggests scattering, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum in her sweater has spilt something, all to keep warm in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splashed' rearranges OUT SO into TOSOU; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot bowl of this red soup is a cosy way of heating up on a cold day.

clue.text: Quiz game ultimately grating

parts.note: to quiz someone is to question them hard, or grill them

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word game

explanation.surface: A quiz game that is, in the end, irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like an adjective meaning annoying; it is the noun, a lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal lattice or screen over a window or opening is a grate of bars.

clue.text: Lovingly played characters recalled during the Roman occupation

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards
characters are letters, here taken from inside the phrase that follows
during says the letters lie within the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: Actors performed with love, recalled from the time Rome occupied Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction meaning 'with love', telling the player to perform tenderly.

clue.text: A poet penning nothing on a ship

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the poet's letters fence in the nothing

parts.note: a bard is a poet
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A poet writing nothing while at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on board a vessel is a direct synonym for being on a ship.

clue.text: Deer with short leg

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a leg of a journey or tournament is a stage

explanation.surface: A deer with a stunted leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, especially an adult red deer, is called this.

clue.text: A bid failing, last of coal seen in mine? That's daunting

indicators.note: seen in says these pieces appear inside another

parts.note: something that is mine is for me

indicators.note: failing suggests going wrong, so these letters are jumbled
last of points to the final letter of the word coal

explanation.surface: A doomed bid in a coal mine looks a frightening prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' turns A BID into IDAB; 'mine' means 'for me', not a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formidable inspires fear or awe by its size or difficulty, just as a daunting task does.

clue.text: Weapons manufacturer has cut hole around bent yew

indicators.note: around says the docked word surrounds the rest
cut means the word is docked of its last letter

parts.note: a bore is a hollow drilled hole, as in a gun's bore

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weaponsmith carving a bent piece of yew with a hole cut through.
explanation.definitionFit: A maker of longbows, traditionally carved from yew, so a craftsman of weapons.

clue.text: See 1
House arrests good for headbanger?

indicators.note: arrests means holds or captures, so the house's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: the House of Hanover was a British royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A royal house detains a decent person on behalf of a heavy-metal fan.
explanation.walkthrough: A headbanger is a heavy-metal fan; cryptically, it is what bangs your head the morning after.
explanation.definitionFit: After heavy drinking one wakes with a pounding headache, so the after-effect is something that bangs the head.

clue.text: Failure to impress Jack in time to get award

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside another

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the failure's letters take the next piece inside

parts.note: a dud is a failure
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A flop fails to impress a man named Jack in time to win a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudge is to grant or confer by a formal decision, as a judge or jury does an award.

clue.text: Girl securing collar on old beast popular with children

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
securing means holding fast, so the girl's letters enclose the next piece

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a ruff is a frilled collar

explanation.surface: A girl fastening a collar on an old animal that children love.
explanation.definitionFit: The monster from Julia Donaldson's picture book is a much-loved children's character.

clue.text: A US composer taken aback, about to leave Spanish guitarist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed letters go round the next piece
taken aback means turned back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: Charles Ives was an American composer
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An American composer, startled, is about to depart from a Spanish guitarist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but turns A plus the composer into SEVIA; Charles Ives is the US composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés Segovia was the celebrated Spanish classical guitarist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Somewhat minimalist hat? I think I expected more!

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone unimpressed by a very plain hat, feeling short-changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A disappointed question asked when something turns out smaller or less impressive than hoped.

clue.text: Looking good, back in US city

parts.note: chic means stylish, looking good
ago means back in time, as in years back

explanation.surface: Someone looking smart again on returning to an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Illinois city on Lake Michigan is a major American metropolis.

clue.text: Bit of a fox on song as features editor

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
a fox's tail is called its brush

explanation.surface: Part of a fox in a song, working as a magazine's features editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features editor' reads as a newspaper job; it is a tool for retouching faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray tool used to retouch photographs, smoothing or altering faces, so it edits people's features.

clue.text: Very famous rich blonde, intoxicating for every heart

indicators.note: for every heart means take the central letters of each word in turn

explanation.surface: A wealthy celebrated blonde whose charms are heady to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely recognised and celebrated as a symbol is described this way, meaning extremely famous.

clue.text: Sheriff once on telly in dereliction of duty, gawped

indicators.note: dereliction means neglect and ruin, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV sheriff stared open-mouthed while neglecting his duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon dog of the 1960s American animated series was a lawman, nominally a sheriff's helper.

clue.text: Ken and Elizabeth tremble in old age

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a well-known British comedian
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Two elderly people, Ken and Elizabeth, shaking with age.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a long-serving Liverpool comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To move shakily and unsteadily, as the frail elderly may, is a synonym.

clue.text: Expressionless seeing something red hot, tipped over coffee

parts.note: a fire poker is something that may be red hot

indicators.note: tipped over means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Someone stays blank-faced on seeing a glowing iron knock over the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A face showing no emotion, as a card player hiding their hand would keep, is blank and unreadable.

clue.text: Respectful title all leaders in Karachi have adopted naturally

indicators.note: all leaders means the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Everyone in charge in Karachi has naturally taken up an honorific.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorific used in South Asia, originally for a ruler, now a respectful name or title.

clue.text: High-flyer in gear change, finally

parts.note: kit is equipment, gear

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word change

explanation.surface: A high achiever who at last switches gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' reads as an achiever; it is literal, something that flies on a string.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy flown high in the wind on a line, and also a soaring bird of prey.

clue.text: I start to panic over something drawn on the turn, duelling weapon?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the first letters are reversed
start to points to the first letter of the word panic
on the turn means reversing, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: lots are drawn to decide something by chance

explanation.surface: Someone about to panic over a drawn weapon as a duel turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns I and P into PI; 'on the turn' turns LOTS into STOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun of the kind used in formal duels, fired at paces apart.

clue.text: Pluck around swallow and head of tropical bird

indicators.note: around says the courage word surrounds the rest

parts.note: grit means courage, pluck
to swallow is to eat

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the word tropical

explanation.surface: Plucking a tropical bird after swallowing its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' and 'bird' tempt you to the swallow as the bird; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A common black-and-yellow European songbird of the titmouse family.
